intro: In the twentieth century, two kinds of movements promised to remake whole societies. On the far left, communists promised equality and an end to exploitation. On the far right, fascists and Nazis promised national glory, order and unity under one leader. Millions of people believed these promises. Tens of millions died under the governments they built.

This unit looks at both extremes with the same care. You will meet a farmer in Ukraine, a teacher in Berlin, students in Beijing and fighters in the Warsaw Ghetto. You will see why people were drawn to these movements, what the regimes did in power, and how people resisted them. You will also meet Hannah Arendt, who argued that the far left and far right shared a new kind of rule.

By the end you will be able to explain the key ideas of communism and fascism, describe their real record with facts and numbers, and compare them fairly. You will also be able to use evidence to argue about why democracies fail and what protects people's rights.
bigQuestion: How did movements that promised a perfect society end in dictatorship and mass murder, and what can protect people from them?

test.q: What did Marx mean by class struggle?
choices: A contest between political parties in elections
Conflict between groups that own property and groups that work for them
test.why: Marx saw history as a struggle between owners and workers.

choices: The Bolshevik seizure of power in Russia
The fall of the Berlin Wall
test.why: The Bolsheviks took power in 1917, before the other events.

choices: Soviet grain seizures and policies that trapped starving peasants
test.why: Human decisions such as high quotas, blacklists and travel bans caused the famine.

choices: Stalin's mass arrests and executions in 1937 and 1938
The Khmer Rouge march out of Phnom Penh
test.why: In 1937 and 1938 about 680,000 people were shot in Stalin's Great Terror.

test.q: Why did the Great Leap Forward lead to famine?
choices: Peasants refused to farm for money
It rained too much for ten years
False harvest reports led the state to take grain people needed
test.why: Frightened officials inflated harvests, and grain was taken based on the false numbers.

choices: Young people who answered Mao's call to attack enemies of the revolution
Soldiers who defended the Berlin Wall
test.why: Red Guards attacked teachers, officials and the Four Olds during the Cultural Revolution.

test.q: About what share of Cambodia's people died under the Khmer Rouge?
test.why: About 1.5 to 2 million died out of roughly 7.8 million people.

test.q: Which statement about Cuba under Castro is fair and balanced?
choices: It had no schools and no hospitals
It expanded schooling and health care but jailed critics and allowed no free elections
It was ruled by the Khmer Rouge
test.why: The chapter names both the gains supporters cite and the lost freedoms critics cite.

test.q: What fears helped Mussolini and Hitler win support?
choices: Fear that the king was too weak to rule
Fear of too much democracy in the USSR
Fear that Japan would invade Europe
Fear of communist revolution and anger over national humiliation
test.why: Strikes, the Depression and the Versailles treaty fed support for both movements.

choices: 1935 laws that stripped German Jews of citizenship
The rules of the Spanish republic
test.why: The Nuremberg Laws took away Jewish citizenship and banned marriages with non-Jews.

test.q: Which was a form of resistance during the Holocaust?
test.why: Jewish fighters in the Warsaw Ghetto held off German troops for nearly a month.

test.q: Which pair of a regime and its leader is correct?
How did Imperial Japan's system differ from Nazi Germany's?
choices: It held free elections with many parties
It was driven by the military and devotion to the emperor, not one party and one dictator
test.why: Militarism, not a single party, drove Japan in the 1930s.

test.q: According to Hannah Arendt, what did totalitarian regimes on the far left and far right share?
choices: Control of every part of life through ideology and terror
The same stated goal of racial conquest
Free elections and a free press
test.why: Arendt argued both used an all-explaining ideology and terror against whole groups.

test.q: What lesson from the century do many scholars agree on?
choices: Unchecked power in the name of a perfect society costs people their rights first
Famines are never caused by governments
Only the far right can become a dictatorship
test.why: Both extremes removed checks on power and then destroyed ordinary rights.

write.prompt: Why did so many people support movements on the far left and far right that ended in dictatorship? Choose one communist regime and one fascist or Nazi regime from the unit. Cite two or three facts or sources, and explain what the two cases share and how they differ.
tips: Name your sources, such as Arendt, the Manifesto or a data table from the unit.
Explain why people were drawn in before you describe what happened.
Treat both extremes with the same care and the same standard of evidence.
Use unit terms such as one-party state, cult of personality and totalitarianism.
Use numbers carefully and say whose estimate they are.
